title: The segmentation fault in malloc_trim(0) when run ASAN
body_html:
The code 1.c :

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <malloc.h>

void* thread_function(void* arg) {
    char* ptr = (char *)malloc(10);
    printf("%p\n", ptr);
    free(ptr);
    malloc_trim(0);
    pthread_exit(NULL);
}

int main() {
    pthread_t threads[2];

    for (long i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
        pthread_create(&threads[i], NULL, thread_function, (void*)i);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
        pthread_join(threads[i], NULL);
    }
    return 0;
}

compile use -fsanitize=address gcc -pthread -o ASANtest -fsanitize=address -O1 1.c And then run ASANtest multiple times. An error occured.

The error information:

If I compile without -fsanitize=address , the program runs normally.

I want to know if the malloc_trim function has any security risks, or if there are any bugs in ASAN

events.body_html: Please don't show images of text. Edit your question to copy-paste the output as text.
Is malloc_trim guaranteed to be thread-safe? Everything from malloc.h is old obsolete gunk, iirc.

On another couple of notes, <malloc.h> is not a standard C heder file. In C you don't need to (and really shouldn't) cast the result of malloc. And if you don't use the thread function argument, pass NULL instead. Oh, and please make sure your code is consistently indented. And don't add things you don't need in your minimal reproducible example (like that unused mutex).
@Someprogrammerdude Well they need it for malloc_trim. But if they actually need malloc_trim is another story.

ASAN works by replacing the malloc family functions, but malloc_trim is a non-standard glibc functionality. Is ASAN even aware of it? I doubt it. Then it wouldn't be surprising that it isn't supported.
In fact yes, @Lundin. The manual page for malloc_trim() says it is thread safe.

@user17732522, you're quite right that malloc_trim() is a glibc extension, and it is indeed plausible that it does not interoperate properly with ASAN. But that would be a bug, on one side or the other, which would be at least a little surprising. Enabling ASAN is not supposed to break correct programs.

As previous commenters said, malloc_trim is a GLIBC extension, which Address Sanitizer knows nothing about.

I just checked: as of this moment malloc_trim is not mentioned at all anywhere in compiler-rt/lib/asan/.

When you call malloc_trim, you get the GLIBC version, which crashes because GLIBC malloc internals have not been initialized (because Address Sanitizer replaces GLIBC malloc).

It would be trivial for ASan developers to intercept malloc_trim and do nothing when it is called, but they probably haven't seen this reported yet.

So do report it in the appropriate bug tracker, and in the mean time you should likely remove all calls to malloc_trim -- it is very unlikely that these calls are doing anything useful in your program.
